events.title: Nationalism and Education in Paraguay, 1870–1954
events.description:
Join us for a lecture from David Rafael Velázquez Seiferheld, which will be delivered in Spanish .

 Empanadas will be served after the presentation .

 David Rafael Velázquez Seiferheld is a professor and researcher at the Metropolitan University of Asunción; the Legislative Academy; and the National University of Villarrica del Espíritu Santo, specializing in Paraguayan history, the history of education, and social history. He has authored numerous academic publications, most notably Mbo’e. Introducción a la historia de la educación paraguaya. His research also encompasses critical documentary analysis from the 18th to the 20th centuries, as well as the study of contemporary political and ideological trajectories. Currently, he is an active member of Paraguayan and international historical research networks and serves as a guest lecturer at various academic forums both in the region and abroad.

Part of the Latin American Studies Presents lecture series.

events.title: The Salvation Army from Imperial Germany to Nazism
events.description:
When the Nazis came to power, the Salvation Army in Germany did something unexpected. Rather than resist, this British-founded outsider organization reshaped its public identity until it was accepted into the Volksgemeinschaft, then reclaimed its international ties after the war and bypassed denazification entirely. Rebecca Carter-Chand uses that history to challenge a common assumption. We expect religious minorities, knowing exclusion firsthand, to extend empathy to other persecuted groups. In Nazi Germany, many did the opposite, seeking the state’s acceptance as a means of self-preservation.

 Rebecca Carter-Chand directs the Programs on Religion and the Holocaust at the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Her book, Christian Internationalism and German Belonging: The Salvation Army from Imperial Germany to Nazism , won the George L. Mosse First Book Prize.

Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."
events.summary: In this lecture, Rebecca Carter-Chand of the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum examines how some religious minorities in Nazi Germany sought the state's acceptance as a means of self-preservation. Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

events.title: Devotional: Rebekka Matheson
events.description:
Rebekka Matheson is an associate professor and course director for the Brain, Behavior, and Movement course in the Department of Preparatory Learning at the BYU School of Medicine. She also serves as the chair of the faculty council of the faculty senate for the school of medicine.

On main campus, she serves as the Associate Director of the Neuroscience Center in the College of Life Sciences, and continues to teach classes for the Neuroscience Center every fall. She co-directs the Neuroscience in Europe International Study Program in spring terms. Matheson graduated from the Neuroscience Center at BYU and then went to medical school at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry, where her clinical and research work emphasized neurology and addiction medicine. While in Rochester, she completed additional graduate coursework in neuropharmacology and physiology. She currently serves in the Relief Society Presidency for the Utah State Hospital branch.

Her remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: 2026 Neal A. Maxwell Lecture
events.description:
The Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship at Brigham Young University presents its Annual Neal A. Maxwell Lecture, commemorating the Institute’s twentieth anniversary and the centennial of Neal A. Maxwell’s birth. Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will speak on “The Limitless Power of Jesus Christ.”

Elder Renlund was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2015. After earning bachelor’s and medical degrees from the University of Utah, he received medical and research training at Johns Hopkins Hospital. He later served as a professor of medicine at the University of Utah and as medical director of the Utah Transplantation Affiliated Hospitals Cardiac Transplant Program. Elder Renlund was born in Salt Lake City, Utah, in November 1952. He married Ruth Lybbert in 1977. They are the parents of one daughter.

This annual lecture honors Elder Neal A. Maxwell’s legacy of faith and intellect by highlighting scholarship that deepens understanding of the restored gospel.

events.title: Devotional: Bishop L. Todd Budge
events.description:
Bishop L. Todd Budge was named First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric on November 14, 2025. Bishop Budge was sustained as a General Authority Seventy on April 6, 2019, and served in that capacity until his call as Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric in October 2020. Bishop Budge has served in a number of Church callings, including stake president, president of the Japan Tokyo Mission, and Area Seventy.

Bishop Budge received a bachelor of arts degree in economics from BYU in 1984. He worked for Bain & Company Japan; Citibank, N.A.; and GE Capital in both Atlanta and Japan. In 2003 he became president and chief executive officer of Tokyo Star Bank Limited; from 2008 to 2011 he served as chairman of the board. He retired from the bank in 2011. During this time, he also served as a member of the board of directors for Hawaiian Airlines.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu
events.summary: Bishop L. Todd Budge was named First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric on November 14, 2025.

Heather Gerken is the 11th president of the Ford Foundation. A nationally recognized expert on democracy, federalism, and elections, Gerken has spent her career working on bipartisan efforts to protect the rule of law.

As president of the Ford Foundation, she leads the $16 billion charitable foundation, which operates offices in the United States and 10 regions around the world.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Joni L. Koch
events.description:
Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch has served in numerous Church callings, including stake president, Area Seventy and president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Responsibilities of Citizenship in a Representative Democracy
events.description:
Spend an evening with Jeff Flake, Wheatley Fellow and former U.S. ambassador, as he speaks about democracy, responsibility, and citizenship.

The event will be held at 7:00 PM in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall.

 

Jeff Flake, who is originally from Snowflake, Arizona, has served in a wide number of public positions. His experience in politics include 12 years as a House Representative and six years as a Senator for the state of Arizona, and roughly two and a half years as U.S. Ambassador to the Republic of Türkiye. He is also the founding Director of the Institute of Politics at Arizona State University, Chairman of the Board of World Trade Center Utah, and a non-resident fellow of Wheatley Institute.

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Alexandra Mackenzie Johns
events.description:
Alexandra Mackenzie Johns will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is an assistant professor of Theatre Arts at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on religious theatre, site-specific performance, verbatim theatre, pilgrimage, and practice-as-research. Johns is known for co-leading the Performance, Religion, and Spirituality group within the International Federation for Theatre Research and for presenting internationally on religious theatre.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.
events.summary: The Wonder of Scripture series invites thoughtful speakers from diverse disciplines to reflect on how sacred texts inspire wonder, deepen understanding, and shape lives.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.location: Hinckley Center Third Floor Lecture Hall
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
events.description:
Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu
